Explanations.ExplanationText: One or more ITR filings were made after the due date
Minimal credit-note reversals — invoiced revenue holds up
Payment bounces detected in bank statements
Young business with limited operating history
Thin cash cushion relative to monthly outflows
Existing EMI obligations consume a large share of inflows
Recurring customers keep paying — sticky counterparty base
No credit bureau record found (New-to-Credit) — this dimension used a neutral default rather than penalizing missing history

Recommendations.RecommendationReason: Entry-tier MUDRA product recommended while financial health improves

Anomaly.Note: Large unexplained gap between GST turnover, ITR income and bank credits — data-integrity signal for officer review, not a creditworthiness deduction.

Ratios.Name: DSCR (Debt Service Coverage)
Ratios.Description: Cash available for debt service vs existing obligations — the primary repayment-capacity test

Ratios.Name: FOIR (Obligations / Inflows)
Ratios.Description: Share of monthly inflows already committed to EMIs — headroom for a new loan

Ratios.Name: Banking Penetration
Ratios.Description: GST-declared sales actually routed through the bank account — cash-sales businesses score low

Ratios.Name: Gross Margin (GST sales vs purchases)
Ratios.Description: Trading margin implied by GSTR-1 outward vs GSTR-2A inward values

Ratios.Name: Days Cash on Hand
Ratios.Description: How long current balances cover average outflows if inflows stopped

Ratios.Name: Inflow Volatility (CV)
Ratios.Description: Month-to-month steadiness of bank inflows — volatile inflows need conservative limits

Ratios.Name: Credit Note Ratio
Ratios.Description: Share of invoiced revenue reversed via credit notes — high values inflate headline turnover

Ratios.Name: GSTR-1 vs GSTR-3B Consistency
Ratios.Description: Agreement between invoice-level (GSTR-1) and summary (GSTR-3B) declared sales — persistent gaps signal misdeclaration

Ratios.Name: ITC Claimed vs 2B Available
Ratios.Description: ITC claimed in GSTR-3B vs auto-drafted availability in GSTR-2B — claiming beyond 2B is an over-claim red flag

Ratios.Name: Supplier Filing Discipline (2B)
Ratios.Description: Share of B2B suppliers whose returns are filed per GSTR-2B — non-filing vendors put the MSME's ITC at risk

Ratios.Name: Profit Before Tax Margin (ITR)
Ratios.Description: Operating profitability from the ITR P&L (AY 2026-27) — profit before tax over turnover

Ratios.Name: Debt to Equity (ITR)
Ratios.Description: Outside liabilities over partners'/members' capital from the ITR balance sheet — how much of the business is funded by borrowing

Ratios.Name: Net Profit Margin (ITR)
Ratios.Description: Bottom-line profitability after all costs and tax, from the ITR P&L

Ratios.Name: Debtor Days (ITR)
Ratios.Description: How long customers take to pay — sundry debtors over turnover × 365 (needs ITR balance sheet)

Ratios.Name: Asset Turnover (ITR)
Ratios.Description: Revenue generated per rupee of assets — turnover over total assets (needs ITR balance sheet)

Notes: Working capital via turnover method: requirement 25% of annual turnover, bank finance 20%, borrower margin 5% (Nayak norms for MSME limits up to ₹5 Cr).
Term capacity assumes 5 year tenure @ 11% p.a., EMI capped at 50% FOIR and 80% of observed monthly surplus.
All amounts scaled by score-band factor 0.35 (AtRisk); indicative only — not a sanction.
Industry: Wholesale and retail trade and repair of motor vehicles (NIC 45) — sector risk weight 0.65 feeds Business Stability; use as a pricing hint, not a sanction condition.
